meta.title: The Settled Science Fair
meta.logline: Kindleton declares all science settled, locks itself indoors over one sneeze and bans exhaling, until Penny builds a booth with a big red button that says Prove Me Wrong.
meta.focus: Book chapter 5: Popper and falsifiability, 'settled science', single-objective optimization in pandemic and climate policy.
meta.source: Ideas from 'Suicidal Empathy: Dying to Be Kind' by Gad Saad (2026), plus published criticism of the book (The Bulwark, Quillette).
meta.disclaimer: Parody and commentary for adults. Strong language. Original characters. Not affiliated with any author, network or show.

lines.text: Scientists at Kindleton University announced today that all science is now settled. Asking further questions is punishable by a fine and a disappointed look.
In related news, the university has fired its scientists, since they're no longer needed. One was seen asking why. He has been fined.

sequence.ticker: ALL QUESTIONS ANSWERED • REMAINING QUESTIONS CONFISCATED • CURIOSITY NOW A CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE

lines.text: Welcome to the Settled Science Fair! This year hypotheses are banned. The answers are already on the wall, and you will love them.
My hypothesis is that hypotheses should be allowed.
Ooh. That's a denier talking. Somebody get the fire extinguisher, she's thinking.
Karl Popper, philosopher, magnificent eyebrows, said a scientific claim has to be falsifiable. It must be possible to prove it wrong.
So, says Saad, settled science is anti-science. Science is never settled. It's just currently winning.
Like a boxing champ.
A champ who has to let anyone climb into the ring. Including that weirdo with the clipboard.
Mayor Hart has declared Operation Zero Sneezes after a man sneezed near the library. Kindleton is now locked down until germs apologize.
Day three hundred. I've named all the furniture. The couch and I are engaged.
Dad, the sneeze guy had hay fever.
Doesn't matter. If it saves just one life...
Grandpa died of boredom. The dog has a podcast. I learned long division from Rocco.
*professorial chitter* (holds up a sponge like chalk)
And to save the planet, cows are banned, cars are banned, and breathing out is strongly discouraged.
We will hit net zero by twenty thirty. Net zero emissions, net zero jobs, net zero fun!
Single-objective optimization. Saad's point about pandemic lockdowns and climate extremism: minimize one number at any cost, and the cost is everything else.
The chapter also wades into gender identity law and women's sport. That's a whole fight of its own. Possibly with helmets.

sequence.title: HEART vs HEAD
sequence.sub: Tonight: trust the science, or test it?

lines.text: Tonight on Heart versus Head: should we trust the science, or test it? I trust whatever gets me off air by nine.
Hal, consensus isn't a conspiracy. When ninety-seven doctors say stop smoking, the three who disagree aren't Galileo. They're usually on a tobacco company's payroll.
Absolutely. Consensus is evidence. It's just not a commandment.
And lockdowns weren't pure madness. Early on nobody knew anything, and some measures saved lives.
Fair. My complaint is pretending there were no trade-offs. Kids' schooling, livelihoods, mental health. Weigh them out loud.
And the do your own research crowd? My cousin did his own research. Now he gargles bleach and owns a horse dewormer subscription.
So. Question everything. Including the bloke questioning everything.
Science, folks. It's complicated. Unlike me. I'm extremely simple.
My project. Here's my claim, here's my data, and here's a big red button that says prove me wrong.
But what if somebody does?
Then I win too. I learn something.
Fine! The lockdown is lifted! But everyone must sneeze into a raccoon.
And finally, Kindleton University has rehired its scientists. Their first finding: the phrase settled science is not settled. Goodnight.
